cards.explanation: The answer is to walk in the LORD's ways. David tells Solomon, "…keep the charge of the LORD your God to walk in His ways and to keep His statutes, commandments, ordinances, and decrees…" (1 Kings 2:3). Solomon, David's son and Israel's king, gets his marching orders, friends, and they come with a long list.

The word is prosper. David says it's "…so that you may prosper in all you do and wherever you turn…" (1 Kings 2:3). And this is a charge about keeping what's written in the Law of Moses, so the way of the whole verse is to follow it. I think David wanted his son to hear that part clearly.

The LORD promised David a man of his line on Israel's throne. David quotes the promise: "…you will never fail to have a man on the throne of Israel." (1 Kings 2:4). The promise is about his descendants sitting on that throne, friends. Here David tells it to his son Solomon as he charges him.

The answer is False. The promise wasn't unconditional. The LORD says, "If your descendants take heed to walk faithfully before Me with all their heart and soul, you will never fail to have a man on the throne of Israel." (1 Kings 2:4). The promise is tied to how David's descendants walk before Him. That little "if" does a lot of work, friends.

Solomon is to not let Joab die in peace. David says, "…do not let his gray head go down to Sheol in peace." (1 Kings 2:6). Sheol is the place of the dead. This is a heavy part of David's charge, friends, and it comes right after he names what Joab did to Abner and Amasa.

The words are loving devotion. David says, "…show loving devotion to the sons of Barzillai the Gileadite…" (1 Kings 2:7). After the heavy part about Joab, this one is a lot warmer, friends. David's instruction for Barzillai's sons is kindness.

The answer is True. David says to "…let them be among those who eat at your table…" (1 Kings 2:7). A seat at the king's table is a warm thing to hand somebody. And David gives his reason: they stood by him when he fled from Absalom.

The answer is True. David says, "…when he came down to meet me at the Jordan, I swore to him by the LORD: ‘I will never put you to the sword.’" (1 Kings 2:8). So David made that promise to Shimei, and he names it out loud to Solomon. Hold that thought, friends, because David isn't done talking about it.

David wants Shimei's gray head brought down to Sheol in blood. He says, "You know what you ought to do to him to bring his gray head down to Sheol in blood." (1 Kings 2:9). Sheol is the place of the dead. This is another heavy part of the charge, friends. David leaves Solomon to use his wisdom.

The number is thirty-three. David reigned "…seven years in Hebron and thirty-three years in Jerusalem." (1 Kings 2:11). Add them up and you get forty years over Israel. I counted it on my mustache twice, friends, and I still needed a minute. This isn't the end of the story, either, because Solomon's kingdom still has more to tell.
